steps.action:
# The Last Light

Old Martin wound the clockwork every night at dusk — had done so for forty years.

On his last night before retirement, a storm rolled in black and furious. He climbed the stairs one final time, joints aching, lantern swaying.

Below, a small fishing boat found its way home through the chaos.

The crew never knew his name. He never knew theirs.

He smiled anyway, and turned off the light for the last time — leaving the automatic beacon to take over.

Some hands you never shake. Some lives you save in the dark.
